# Purpose

This problem develops load-path reasoning, power-to-torque conversion, internal torque, torsional shear stress, shaft sizing, standard-size selection, and engineering judgment. Award credit for a correct torque load path, consistent power and speed units, the solid-shaft torsion relation, upward standard-size selection, stress verification, and a recommendation bounded by the assumptions of the model.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The base model assumes steady operation, a uniform solid circular shaft, linear-elastic material behavior, pure torsion, negligible shaft self-weight, negligible bearing friction, and constant transmitted power. Belt-induced bending, transverse bearing reactions, keyways, stress concentrations, shock loading, fatigue, critical speed, coupling details, and manufacturing tolerances require additional models and data.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation: 10%;
- structural idealization and assumptions: 15%;
- power, speed, and torque calculation: 20%;
- torsional-stress sizing: 30%;
- standard-size selection and verification: 15%;
- engineering recommendation and limitations: 10%.
